purpose: Third-party recognition programs usable as inclusion criteria and as citable provenance tags. An award is a BOOTSTRAP signal: it bounds a starting list and indicates kitchen competence. It does NOT predict whether a kitchen will accommodate a low-protein diet, and the guide must never imply that it does.
usage_rule: Store and display: program name, tier label VERBATIM from the program, edition/year, and a source URL. Never store or display the program's descriptive prose about the restaurant -- that is their copyright. Facts plus a citation only.

programs.name: MICHELIN Guide
programs.tier_note: 'Selected' is the current term for the non-starred, non-Bib tier. 'Recommended' appears in press and in some legislative citations but is legacy usage. Store the program's own current word.
programs.geographic_coverage: ~40 destinations, heavily Europe/Japan/US-coastal weighted. Sparse in Africa, South Asia, Latin America, most of the US interior.
programs.access_note: guide.michelin.com returns 403 to non-browser clients. Their bot policy; capture in a browser.
programs.ip_posture: Famous mark, active enforcer. French operator, so EU database right (Directive 96/9/EC) plausibly attaches to systematic worldwide extraction of the selection. Word mark only, plain text, no Bibendum/roundel/star glyphs.

programs.name: James Beard Foundation Awards
programs.tier_note: Chef- and restaurant-level, by category and region. A semifinalist nod is a real signal and is far more common than a Michelin mention in the US interior.
programs.ip_posture: US non-profit. Word mark; same referential-use discipline.

programs.name: The World's 50 Best Restaurants
programs.geographic_coverage: Global but extremely thin -- hundreds of restaurants worldwide.

programs.name: Gault&Millau
programs.geographic_coverage: Continental Europe, strong in France/Benelux/DACH. Useful where Michelin is thin.

programs.name: La Liste
programs.geographic_coverage: Global, ~1000+ per edition. Aggregates other guides, so coverage is broader than any single one.
programs.ip_posture: Aggregator, so its own rights claim is over the compilation.

programs.name: Local press and city-magazine best-of lists
programs.geographic_coverage: Universal -- every city has one. This is the real horizontal-coverage tag.
programs.ip_posture: Many small publishers. Individually low risk, collectively unmanageable for permissions. Cite and link; store no prose.
programs.revised_note: Upgraded from 'unlimited coverage, variable quality'. The variable-quality problem is solved by harvesting CATEGORIES rather than winners: 'Best Tapas' carries real structural information about a menu, 'Best Restaurant' carries none. Roughly 15-18 of the several hundred categories in a typical reader poll map onto signals.

programs.name: PKU Commons community nomination
programs.ip_posture: Ours. No third-party rights, no attribution burden, no takedown exposure.
programs.note: The strategically important row. Every other program is someone else's list that we cite; this one is ours, has no IP surface, and is the only tag whose coverage grows with the community rather than with a publisher's travel budget.

design_conclusion: Awards are ONE inclusion criterion among several, stored as citable provenance. A guide organized around a single award program inherits that program's legal surface and its coverage gaps, and implies a predictive relationship the census data will contradict.

changelog.change: Added the Asheville local-list instance and the category-harvesting method. Recorded that a membership organization (AIR) outranks every award list for this guide's purposes, because it supplies access rather than names.
